message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"specific","gloss":"a specific (a medicine for one particular disease)","category":"specific","note":"Jowett writes 'it is a specific both for the memory and for the wit'. The word has medical overtones but is narrower than 'remedy' or 'drug', and it loses the ambivalence of remedy/poison."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"the memory","gloss":"the memory","note":"Preceded by 'better memories' in the previous clause, which renders μνημονικωτέρους. Here 'the memory' renders μνήμης."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"the wit","gloss":"the wit (intelligence)","note":"σοφίας is rendered as 'wit', which is a weaker and more intellectual-faculty sense than 'wisdom'. This is not the same word Jowett uses at 275a, where he writes 'truth' and 'semblance of truth' instead of wisdom."},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"specific","gloss":"specific (a medicine for one particular disease)","category":"specific","note":"'The specific which you have discovered' keeps the same word as at 274e."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"'an aid not to memory'. Jowett turns the genitive into a dative-like 'to memory' and makes the pharmakon an 'aid', which changes the syntax."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"reminiscence","gloss":"reminiscence (recollection)","note":"'but to reminiscence'. This is Platonic-sounding (anamnesis-like) rather than 'reminding' or 'prompting', so it blurs the contrast between internal recollection and external reminder."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"the semblance of truth","gloss":"the semblance (likeness) of truth","note":"Jowett paraphrases: 'not truth, but only the semblance of truth'. σοφίας ... δόξαν is not rendered as 'wisdom'. The word 'wisdom' is absent here, and the idea is recast as truth-semblance. 'Wisdom' appears only later, in 'the show of wisdom'."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"the show of wisdom","gloss":"the show (appearance) of wisdom","note":"'having the show of wisdom without the reality' renders δοξόσοφοι γεγονότες ἀντὶ σοφῶν. The compound adjective for persons, 'wise-seeming', becomes an abstract noun phrase, and 'without the reality' replaces ἀντὶ σοφῶν."},"argument":"Jowett keeps one word, 'specific', for both occurrences of φάρμακον, so Thamus does turn Theuth's own word back on him, but a narrow medical term replaces the ambivalent drug/remedy/poison sense, so the possible poison reading is lost. He also gives 'wit' for σοφία at 274e and 'truth' and 'reality' at 275a-b, which weakens the wisdom/seeming-wisdom contrast, and he renders 'reminiscence' for ὑπομνήσεως, so the memory/reminder opposition is partly blurred. The exchange reads as a dispute over whether the cure fits the ailment rather than whether the remedy is also a poison."}
